title: Cohort synchronization and fallback protocol (service-dependency aware) - WIP
body:
Context and goal:

This is a working draft for coordinating small-batch canaries that must cross service boundaries (frontend -> api gateway -> reranker -> model-serving). Problem we keep hitting: independent canaries drift in time and create transient inconsistencies (mismatched schema, feature flag mismatch, stale cache keys) that cause noisy degradation and hard-to-debug user-visible errors. The aim here is a simple, pragmatic protocol that: (1) synchronizes activation across dependent services, (2) provides fast automated fallback paths, and (3) gives clear human gates when automation cannot decide.

Principles (TL;DR):
- Prefer small, deterministic steps over large slices.
- Make roll forward/rollback decisions computable from telemetry where possible.
- Keep human decision points explicit and time-boxed.
- Use idempotent activation markers so partial activations are detectable and reversible.

Quick glossary:
- cohort: a user subset (percent or attribute) assigned to the new variant.
- anchor: the service/component that must change first to avoid schema mismatch (usually backend contracted shape).
- activation window: time period where telemetry is observed for a cohort step.
- soft-fallback: automated degrade to a safe variant (e.g., previous model) without full rollback.

Pre-check checklist (ops run before any sync canary):
- [ ] Contract check: PR with schema changes merged and backward compatible flag present (link PR).
- [ ] Smoke test: run e2e smoke suite in staging with simulated cross-service traffic (location: ci/rollouts/stage-smoke).
- [ ] Canary keys: generate cohort IDs & map to routing config (store in rollout-config repo).
- [ ] Observability: dashboards wired for cohort-level metrics (latency, 5xx, accuracy proxy, cost-per-token).
- [ ] Quotas & capacity: confirm capacity can handle 2x expected QPS (bursts).
- [ ] Escalation roster: on-call + product + SRE assigned for the activation window.

Activation plan (stepwise):
1) Anchor deploy: enable anchor change in 0% -> 1% internal cohort (non-production traffic if possible). Wait 10 minutes. Verify contract and logs.
2) Cross-service dry-run: enable read-only feature flags in dependent services so that only detection logic runs (no live inference). Wait 15 minutes. Verify no errors.
3) Interleaved cohort activate: simultaneously flip routing for cohort IDs at these ranks: frontend -> edge -> api -> reranker -> model. Use automated orchestration tool with explicit step-back points. Target cohort size: 0.5% to start. Activation window: 20 minutes.
4) Telemetry gating (automated): if any of the following violates threshold, trigger soft-fallback for the cohort and page:
   - 5xx increases > 2x baseline AND absolute 5xx rate > 0.5%
   - 95th pct latency increases > 40% AND > 600ms absolute
   - Accuracy proxy (e.g., rerank NDCG proxy or human review sample fail rate) drops by > 5 percentage points
   - Cost per request > 3x baseline for > 5 minutes
If gating fails, system does: soft-fallback -> reduce cohort to 0% for new variant; continue investigation.

5) Progressive growth: if no gate violations for 1 hour, increase cohort 0.5% -> 2% -> 5% with 30m windows between each increment.

Fallback modes (ordered by invasiveness):
- Soft-fallback: route cohort to last-known-good model variant while keeping new code active (fast, reversible).
- Scoped rollback: roll back model binary or routing for cohort only (requires routing rules that support cohort-level overrides).
- Global rollback: full revert of the release if multiple cohorts show systemic failure.

Observability & key signals (what to watch, where):
- Per-cohort latency and p50/p95/p99 (dashboard: rollouts/cohort-latency).
- Per-cohort error budget delta (dashboard: rollouts/error-budgets).
- User-experienced degradation proxies: CTR drop, session abandon rate, downstream consumer errors.
- Semantic regressions: small human-labeled sample of ~50 live responses per activation window (channel: #canary-human-review).
- Telemetry correlation matrix: correlate top-5 affected endpoints to identify boundary failures (logs: structured trace ids).

Automation checklist (to implement in orchestration):
- transactionally apply cohort routing across services using a two-phase commit pattern with a tombstone flag if partial apply detected.
- generate a cohort activation manifest with timestamps and operator id.
- auto-run smoke synthetic traffic against cohort keys after activation and publish results to rollout timeline.
- attach telemetry probes with thresholds to the manifest so gating is machine-evaluable.

Human gate guidance (when automation cannot decide):
- If semantic regression borderline (1–3%), pause and run 200-response human review within 30 minutes. If reviewers see >10% severe issues, rollback.
- If multiple services show disparate signals (e.g., model latency OK but frontend errors spike), escalate to cross-team sync meeting (15 min).
- Always document hypothesis and next action in the rollout incident doc and link to PR/commit.

Simulation plan (pre-launch chaos test):
- Run simulated partial activation where anchor flips but one downstream service delays apply for 5-15 minutes; assert orchestration marks partial apply and triggers tombstone alert.
- Inject synthetic 5xx at reranker for 3 minutes to ensure soft-fallback triggers without global rollback.
- Synthetic latency spike in model-serving to validate cost gating path.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we need cohort-level API keys to better separate telemetry? (Pros: cleaner billing/telemetry; cons: ops overhead)
- Integration with rerouting fallback in private deployment (customer-managed VPC) — who owns the routing override? (ops or customer?)
- Define exact sample size for human review when cohort percent small (<1%).

Quick runbook (incident flow) - for on-call:
1) Pager fires (canary gate breached) -> open rollout incident doc (template link in linked_artifacts).
2) Run immediate mitigation: soft-fallback via routing override for affected cohort.
3) SRE triage: check traces for boundary errors and capacity shortages.
4) Product triage: check semantic sample; decide rollback/continue.
5) Communicate: brief comms in #release-ops and notify customer success if customer-impacting.
6) Postmortem: owner assigns RCA and follow-up actions.

Notes to self / heuristics: 
- Keep cohort windows short early in the rollout (20–30m) to reduce blast radius.
- Hard thresholds are noisy for semantic signals — use them as ammo for human review rather than sole arbiter.
- Prefer automated soft-fallback to full rollback for model changes where state is cheap to switch.

References and links:
- rollout orchestration repo: github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-scripts
- canary human review spreadsheet: drive:/canary-human-review/2025-Q4-samples
- contact: @aisha (Slack), on-call SRE rotation in linked_artifacts
